arxiv-2012-03512.title: The Fictitious Domain Method Based on Navier Slip Boundary Condition for Simulation of Flow-Particle Interaction Journal: Elsevier
arxiv-2012-03512.creator: Rong Zhang, Qiaolin He
arxiv-2012-03512.description: Abstract In this article, we develop a least–squares/fictitious domain method for direct simulation of fluid particle motion with Navier slip boundary condition at the fluid–particle interface. Let Ω \Omega and B B be two bounded domains of ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} such that B ¯ ⊂ Ω \overline{B}\subset\Omega . The motion of solid particle B B is governed by Newton’s equations.

arxiv-2101-07607.title: Asymptotic behavior of the number of distinct values in a sample from the geometric stick-breaking process
arxiv-2101-07607.creator: Pierpaolo De Blasi, Ramsés H. Mena, Igor Prünster
arxiv-2101-07607.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pierpaolo De Blasi, Ramsés H. Mena, Igor Prünster. Discrete random probability measures are a key ingredient of Bayesian nonparametric inferential procedures. A sample generates ties with positive probability and a fundamental object of both theoretical and applied interest is the corresponding random number of distinct values. The growth rate can be determined from the rate of decay of the small frequencies implying that, when the decreasingly ordered frequencies admit a tractable form, the asymptotics of the number of distinct values can be conveniently assessed.

arxiv-2110-06444.title: Large deviation principles for SDEs under locally weak monotonicity conditions
arxiv-2110-06444.creator: Jian Wang Hao Yang Jianliang Zhai Tusheng Zhang 1. School of Mathematical Sciences, University of Science and Technology of China,Hefei, Anhui 230026, China.2. Department of Mathematics, University of Manchester,Oxford Road, Manchester, M13 9PL, UK.
arxiv-2110-06444.description: Abstract \theorembodyfont Abstract: This paper establishes a Freidlin-Wentzell large deviation principle for stochastic differential equations(SDEs) under locally weak monotonicity conditions and Lyapunov conditions. We illustrate the main result of the paper by showing that it can be applied to SDEs with non-Lipschitzian coefficients, which can not be covered in the existing literature.

arxiv-2201-12840.title: Maximal estimates for Weyl sums on 𝕋 d \mathbb{T}^{d}
arxiv-2201-12840.creator: Changxing Miao, Jiye Yuan, Tengfei Zhao
arxiv-2201-12840.description: Abstract . In this paper, we obtain the maximal estimate for the Weyl sums on the torus 𝕋 d \mathbb{T}^{d} with d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 , which is sharp up to the endpoint. We also consider two variants of this problem which include the maximal estimate along the rational lines and on the generic torus.

arxiv-2205-13249.title: DT-SV: A Transformer-based Time-domain Approach for Speaker Verification Thanks: † Corresponding Author: Jianzong Wang, jzwang@188.com
arxiv-2205-13249.creator: Nan Zhang, Jianzong Wang † , Zhenhou Hong, Chendong Zhao, Xiaoyang Qu, Jing Xiao
arxiv-2205-13249.description: Abstract Speaker verification (SV) aims to determine whether the speaker’s identity of a test utterance is the same as the reference speech. In the past few years, extracting speaker embeddings using deep neural networks for SV systems has gone mainstream. Recently, different attention mechanisms and Transformer networks have been explored widely in SV fields.

arxiv-2205-14323.title: Multi-agent Databases via Independent Learning (Extended Abstract)
arxiv-2205-14323.creator: Chi Zhang, Olga Papaemmanouil, Josiah P. Hanna, Aditya Akella
arxiv-2205-14323.description: Abstract . Machine learning is rapidly being used in database research to improve the effectiveness of numerous tasks including but not limited to query optimization, workload scheduling and physical design. Currently, the research focus has been on replacing a single database component responsible for one task with its learning-based counterpart.

arxiv-2207-09107.title: MONet: Multi-scale Overlap Network for Duplication Detection in Biomedical Images
arxiv-2207-09107.creator: Ekraam Sabir, Soumyaroop Nandi, Wael AbdAlmageed, Prem Natarajan
arxiv-2207-09107.description: Abstract Manipulation of biomedical images to misrepresent experimental results has plagued the biomedical community for a while. Recent interest in the problem led to the curation of a dataset and associated tasks to promote the development of biomedical forensic methods. Of these, the largest manipulation detection task focuses on the detection of duplicated regions between images.

arxiv-2209-06016.title: Magnetic-Field Induced Deformation in Hybrid Stars
arxiv-2209-06016.creator: Ishfaq A. Rather, Asloob A. Rather, Ilídio Lopes, V. Dexheimer, A. A. Usmani, S. K. Patra
arxiv-2209-06016.description: Abstract The effects of strong magnetic fields on the deconfinement phase transition expected to take place in the interior of massive neutron stars are studied in detail for the first time. For hadronic matter, the very general density-dependent relativistic mean-field (DD-RMF) model is employed, while the simple, but effective vector-enhanced bag model (vBag) model is used to study quark matter.

arxiv-2404-07258.title: Complete Optimal Non-Resonant Anomaly Detection
arxiv-2404-07258.creator: Gregor Kasieczka, John Andrew Raine, David Shih, Aman Upadhyay
arxiv-2404-07258.description: Abstract We propose the first-ever complete, model-agnostic search strategy based on the optimal anomaly score, for new physics on the tails of distributions. Signal sensitivity is achieved via a classifier trained on auxiliary features in a weakly-supervised fashion, and backgrounds are predicted using the ABCD method in the classifier output and the primary tail feature.

arxiv-2404-14908.title: Mining Supervision for Dynamic Regions in Self-Supervised Monocular Depth Estimation
arxiv-2404-14908.creator: Hoang Chuong Nguyen, Tianyu Wang, Jose M. Alvarez, Miaomiao Liu
arxiv-2404-14908.description: Abstract This paper focuses on self-supervised monocular depth estimation in dynamic scenes trained on monocular videos. Existing methods jointly estimate pixel-wise depth and motion, relying mainly on an image reconstruction loss. Dynamic regions 1 1 1 Dynamic regions indicate regions covered by moving objects.

arxiv-2405-18677.title: Zero-to-Hero: Enhancing Zero-Shot Novel View Synthesis via Attention Map Filtering
arxiv-2405-18677.creator: Ido Sobol 1 Chenfeng Xu 2 Or Litany 1,3
arxiv-2405-18677.description: Abstract Generating realistic images from arbitrary views based on a single source image remains a significant challenge in computer vision, with broad applications ranging from e-commerce to immersive virtual experiences. Recent advancements in diffusion models, particularly the Zero-1-to-3 model, have been widely adopted for generating plausible views, videos, and 3D models.

arxiv-2501-09780.title: MUSE observations of V1425 Aql reveal an arc-shaped nova shell.
arxiv-2501-09780.creator: Lientur Celedón, Claus Tappert, Linda Schmidtobreick, Fernando J. Selman
arxiv-2501-09780.description: Abstract Context. Nova shells are the remnants of a nova eruption in a cataclysmic variable system. By studying their geometry we can better understand the physical mechanisms that shape them during the nova eruption. A nova shell that challenges our current understanding of these processes is the shell observed around V1425 Aql.

arxiv-2502-15539.title: PtrHash: Minimal Perfect Hashing at RAM Throughput
arxiv-2502-15539.creator: Ragnar Groot Koerkamp
arxiv-2502-15539.description: Abstract Motivation. Given a set K K of n n keys, a minimal perfect hash function (MPHF) is a collision-free bijective map 𝖧 𝗆𝗉𝗁𝖿 \mathsf{H_{mphf}} from K K to { 0 , … , n − 1 } \{0,\dots,n-1\} .

arxiv-2504-05617.title: PASSAGES: The Discovery of a Strongly Lensed Protocluster Core Candidate at Cosmic Noon
arxiv-2504-05617.creator: Nicholas Foo, Kevin C. Harrington, Brenda L. Frye, Patrick S. Kamieneski, Min S. Yun, Massimo Pascale, Ilsang Yoon, Allison Noble, Rogier A. Windhorst, Seth H. Cohen, James D. Lowenthal, Melanie Kaasinen, Belén Alcalde Pampliega, Daizhong Liu, Olivia Cooper, Carlos Garcia Diaz, Anastasio Díaz-Sánche
arxiv-2504-05617.description: Abstract Investigating the processes by which galaxies rapidly build up their stellar mass during the peak of their star formation ( z = 2 − 3 z=2-3 ) is crucial to advancing our understanding of the assembly of large-scale structures.

arxiv-2505-06802.title: Upper Limit of Electron Energization in the Near-Earth Plasma Sheet during Substorm Injections
arxiv-2505-06802.creator: Weiqin Sun, Xiao-Jia Zhang, Anton V. Artemyev, Xi Lu, Xinlin Li, Yang Mei, Zheng Xiang, Declan O’Brien
arxiv-2505-06802.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Weiqin Sun, Xiao-Jia Zhang, Anton V. Artemyev, Xi Lu, Xinlin Li, Yang Mei, Zheng Xiang, Declan O’Brien. The Earth’s magnetotail, located on the night side of the magnetosphere, is a dynamic region where magnetic field energy is released and converted into plasma heating, particle acceleration, and kinetic energy through magnetic reconnection. Recent low-altitude observations from the CIRBE CubeSat reveal that the efficiency of particle acceleration in the magnetotail can be high enough to produce relativistic and ultra-relativistic electrons with energies reaching several MeV.

arxiv-2505-14742.title: Quaff: Quantized Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning under Outlier Spatial Stability Hypothesis
arxiv-2505-14742.creator: Hong Huang, Dapeng Wu
arxiv-2505-14742.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Hong Huang, Dapeng Wu. Large language models (LLMs) have made exciting achievements across various domains, yet their deployment on resource-constrained personal devices remains hindered by the prohibitive computational and memory demands of task-specific fine-tuning. While quantization offers a pathway to efficiency, existing methods struggle to balance performance and overhead, either incurring high computational/memory costs or failing to address activation outliers, a critical bottleneck in quantized fine-tuning.

arxiv-2507-03843.title: Regularizing Log-Linear Cost Models for Inpatient Stays by Merging ICD-10 Codes
arxiv-2507-03843.creator: Chi-Ken Lu, David Alonge, Nicole Richardson, Bruno Richard
arxiv-2507-03843.description: Abstract Cost models in healthcare research must balance interpretability, accuracy, and parameter consistency. However, interpretable models often struggle to achieve both accuracy and consistency. Ordinary least squares (OLS) models for high-dimensional regression can be accurate but fail to produce stable regression coefficients over time when using highly granular ICD-10 diagnostic codes as predictors.

arxiv-2601-11838.title: SimFuzz: Similarity-guided Block-level Mutation for RISC-V Processor Fuzzing
arxiv-2601-11838.creator: Hao Lyu , Jingzheng Wu ✉ , Xiang Ling ✉ , Yicheng Zhong , Zhiyuan Li , Tianyue Luo
arxiv-2601-11838.description: Abstract The Instruction Set Architecture (ISA) defines processor operations and serves as the interface between hardware and software. As an open ISA, RISC-V lowers the barriers to processor design and encourages widespread adoption, but also exposes processors to security risks such as functional bugs. Processor fuzzing is a powerful technique for automatically detecting these bugs.

plos-pone-0006486.title: GDNF Selectively Induces Microglial Activation and Neuronal Survival in CA1/CA3 Hippocampal Regions Exposed to NMDA Insult through Ret/ERK Signalling
plos-pone-0006486.creator: Francesca Boscia, Carla Lucia Esposito, Antonella Di Crisci et al.
plos-pone-0006486.description: PLOS ONE research article. The glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF) is a potent survival factor for several neuronal populations in different brain regions, including the hippocampus. However, no information is available on the: (1) hippocampal subregions involved in the GDNF-neuroprotective

pmc-10506629.title: Characterization of sulfur/carbon copolymer cathodes for Li–S batteries: a combined experimental and ab initio Raman spectroscopy study†
pmc-10506629.creator: Rana Kiani, Matthias Steimecke, Marah Alqaisi, Michael Bron, Daniel Sebastiani, Pouya Partovi-Azar
pmc-10506629.description: Optimization of lithium–sulfur batteries highly depends on exploring and characterizing new cathode materials. Sulfur/carbon copolymers have recently attracted much attention as an alternative class of cathodes to replace crystalline sulfur. In particular, poly(sulfur-n-1,3-diisopropenylbenzene) (S/DIB) has been under considerable experimental and theoretical investigations, promising a good performance in mitigating the so-called shuttle effect.

pmc-10616940.title: Effectiveness of an Educational Workshop on Palliative Care Knowledge in Lebanese Nurses
pmc-10616940.creator: Myrna AA Doumit, May Naifeh Khoury, Mary Arevian, Ghina Al Khatib, Suha Fares
pmc-10616940.description: Background:Lebanon is one of the world's smallest countries, with an area of 10,452 square kilometers. Life expectancy in Lebanon presently stands at about 76.6 years for men and 79.3 years for women. It is well known that with long life comes chronic disease, serious illness, and increased resource utilization.

pmc-10649593.title: Mechanical Performance and Failure Analysis of a 3D-Printed “Continuous Layer–Lattice Layer–Continuous Layer” Sandwich Structure
pmc-10649593.creator: Daming Nie, Lingyu Kong, Yu Zhang, Xingyu Qiu, Yili Fu, Jason Gu, Amir Ameli
pmc-10649593.description: Sandwich structures are engineered with continuous layers surrounding the inner lattices, which combines the advantages of the high strength of the continuous layer and the light weight of the lattice layer. They are widely employed in weight-critical energy-absorbing engineering fields such as aerospace, automobile, and robotics.

pmc-11477850.title: Prenylated Dihydroflavonol from Sophora flavescens Regulate the Polarization and Phagocytosis of Macrophages In Vitro
pmc-11477850.creator: Lu Su, Kairui Rao, Lizhong Wang, Li Pu, Zhijun Zhang, Hongmei Li, Rongtao Li, Dan Liu, Francisco Leon
pmc-11477850.description: As an important member of innate immunity, macrophages show remarkable plasticity and heterogeneity, and play an important role in immune regulation, tissue development, homeostasis of the internal environment and injury repair. However, the excessive activation of macrophages is closely related to the occurrence and development of many diseases.

pmc-11522187.title: The role of evaluatively conditioned stimuli in iconic memory
pmc-11522187.creator: Alexandra E Clausen, Florian Kattner
pmc-11522187.description: In the present study, an attempt was made to replicate results found about the influence of valence on prioritisation and decay in iconic memory. Hereby, the evaluative conditioning effect was used to induce valence for formerly neutral stimuli. The effect is gained by pairing neutral stimuli with either positive, negative, or neutral images in a conditioning phase.

pmc-12270267.title: The Replication Database: Documenting the Replicability of Psychological Science
pmc-12270267.creator: Lukas Röseler, Leonard Kaiser, Christopher Doetsch, Noah Klett, Christian Seida, Astrid Schütz, Balazs Aczel, Nadia Adelina, Valeria Agostini, Samuel Alarie, Nihan Albayrak-Aydemir, Alaa Aldoh, Ali H. Al-Hoorie, Flavio Azevedo, Bradley J. Baker, Charlotte Lilian Barth, Julia Beitner, Cameron Brick,
pmc-12270267.description: In psychological science, replicability—repeating a study with a new sample achieving consistent results (Parsons et al., 2022)—is critical for affirming the validity of scientific findings. Despite its importance, replication efforts are few and far between in psychological science with many attempts failing to corroborate past findings.

pmc-12722296.title: Sit to stand and timed up and go in idiopathic inflammatory myopathies
pmc-12722296.creator: Tanya Chandra, Raisa L Silva, Shiri Keret, Runjia Li, G K Balasubramani, Ramsha Riaz, Akanksha Sharma, Jesse Wilkerson, Dana P Ascherman, Chester V Oddis, Siamak Moghadam-Kia, Rohit Aggarwal
pmc-12722296.description: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies can significantly impair physical function, of which Sit to Stand (STS) and Timed Up and Go (TUG) are quick, operator independent measures. We aimed to evaluate psychometric properties of STS and TUG compared to established core set measures of disease activity; and assess feasibility of patients self-performing these tests remotely.

pmc-13431069.title: Assessing Multi-Modal Imaging for Late Capsular Bag Distension Syndrome: A Study of Two Clinical Cases
pmc-13431069.creator: Gizem Dogan Gokce, Gamze Ozkan, Semra Akkaya Turhan
pmc-13431069.description: We report two cases of late capsular bag distension syndrome (LCBDS), which is a rare but significant complication following cataract surgery and often presents with blurred vision years after intraocular lens (IOL) implantation. Case 1: An 80-year-old male presented with a one-year history of progressive blurred vision in the right eye.

pmc-13439317.title: Abnormal auditory neural activity in individuals with spinal muscular atrophy
pmc-13439317.creator: Gary Rance, Eppie M Yiu
pmc-13439317.description: Spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by hypotonia, progressive muscle weakness and atrophy caused by progressive loss of motor neurons in the spinal cord and lower cranial nerve nuclei. The disease has also been associated with sensory neuropathies affecting the visual, somatosensory and auditory pathways.
